analysis: The code snippet contains a loop that iterates over a list `vals` using an index `i` that goes from 0 to `vals.size()-1`. The call `vals.get(i)` is made inside the loop. The API documentation for `get` indicates that it throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if the index is out of range (i.e., `index < 0 || index >= size()`). The loop condition `i < vals.size()` guarantees that `i` is always less than the size of the list, and `i` starts at 0 and increments, so it is never negative. Therefore, the condition for `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is never satisfied in this context. The exception is fully avoided.
remark: The loop condition `i < vals.size()` ensures that the index passed to `get(i)` is always within the valid range [0, size-1], so no `IndexOutOfBoundsException` can occur from any `get` call in the snippet.
